children: Indian government bonds could rise marginally in opening deals on Wednesday, after the benchmark bond yield slid six basis points in the first two sessions of the week, tracking a decline in oil prices and as Treasury yields did not rise after a point.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 7.00% and 7.05%, according to a trader with a primary dealership.
It ended at 7.0106% in the previous session, after closing at 7.0686% on Friday.
"Though the buying oozed some confidence yesterday, the 10-year bond yield below 7% at the current juncture may be a wishful thinking," the trader added.

Oil prices fell on Tuesday for the fifth straight session and were nearly unchanged in Asian hours on increasing flows of crude from Saudi Arabia, with the restart of the East-West pipeline and ship movements through the Strait of Hormuz.
Still, declines were curbed after U.S. President Donald Trump said a peace deal would come after the US mid-term elections in early November, and without a peace deal he could "annihilate" Iran.

India, which imports roughly 90% of its crude oil needs, is particularly exposed to swings in global oil prices, with elevated oil prices and a weak monsoon raising inflation concerns and expectations of an interest rate hike in the next two weeks.

Policy tightening bets in India have hardened after August retail inflation stood at 4.82% and the Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points last week, which was its first such move since 2023.
The Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision is due on October 7, with the majority of market participants now moving towards a repo rate hike.
Meanwhile, the 10-year Treasury yield continued to move in a narrow range of 4.95%-5.00%, with the higher range acting as a strong ceiling.
Overnight indexed swap rates are expected to be range-bound.
The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.0625%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) rate closed at 6.2550% and the five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate settled at 6.5125%.
